tip: Запомни (zapomni = remember) is the informal command to one person. For formal or plural, add -те: запомните (zapomnite).
сюда (syuda = to here) marks motion toward the speaker. A static location would use здесь (zdes = here) instead.
Давайте (davayte = let's) plus a perfective we-form makes a suggestion: Давайте закончим (davayte zakonchim = let's finish).
мне (mne = to me) is the dative of я, marking who gets shown something: покажите мне (pokazhite mne = show me).
лучшая (luchshaya = best) is the irregular superlative of хороший (khoroshiy = good), not a самый form.
становится (stanovitsya = becomes) plus a comparative like теплее (teplee = warmer) expresses a gradual change.
гораздо (gorazdo = much) intensifies a comparative: гораздо интереснее (gorazdo interesnee = much more interesting).
After a comparative, the thing compared goes in the genitive: важнее работы (vazhnee raboty = more important than work).
работать (rabotat = to work) plus the instrumental names a job: работает врачом (rabotaet vrachom = works as a doctor).
Numbers 2, 3, 4 take a genitive singular noun: три комнаты (tri komnaty = three rooms), not the plural form.
For equal comparison use такой же ... как (takoy zhe ... kak = as ... as): такой же высокий (takoy zhe vysokiy = just as tall).
которую (kotoruyu = that/which) is feminine accusative here, matching книга (kniga = book) as the object being read.
With one subject, чтобы (chtoby = in order to) takes the infinitive: чтобы успеть (chtoby uspet = in order to make it).
Negative commands take the imperfective verb: Не сдавайся (Ne sdavaysya = don't give up), not the perfective form.
When the comparison is a whole clause, use чем (chem = than): сильнее, чем выглядит (silnee, chem vyglyadit = stronger than she looks).
более (bolee = more) plus a plain adjective forms a comparative: более опытный (bolee opytnyy = more experienced).
самый (samyy = most) before an adjective builds the superlative: самый высокий (samyy vysokiy = the tallest).
The по- prefix on a comparative softens it to 'a bit more': поудобнее (poudobnee = a bit more comfortable).
A comparative plus всех (vsekh = than all) means best of the group: быстрее всех (bystree vsekh = faster than everyone).
The frame Чем ... тем ... (chem ... tem ... = the more ... the more) links two comparatives: Чем дальше, тем больше (chem dalshe, tem bolshe).
по-русски (po-russki = in Russian) is the set adverb for speaking a language: говорит по-русски (govorit po-russki = speaks Russian).
To say someone is absent, use нет plus the genitive: меня нет (menya net = I'm not here, I'm away).
